text: Definition 1 (Population directional objective) . The population counterpart of the empirical CRN objective is $\psi(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau}[\phi_{i}(s)],$ where the expectation is taken with respect to the distribution used to generate the empirical objective.

Assumption 1 (Pathwise smoothness) . For each example $\tau_{i}$ , the per-sample directional objective $\phi_{i}$ is five times continuously differentiable on the interval $[-\epsilon,R]$ : $\phi_{i}\in C^{5}([-\epsilon,R]).$

Assumption 2 (Higher-order derivative bounds) . There exist constants $W,M,B,L>0$ such that, for every $i$ and every $s\in[-\epsilon,R]$ , $|\phi_{i}^{\prime\prime}(s)|\leq W,$ $|\phi_{i}^{\prime\prime\prime}(s)|\leq M,$ $|\phi_{i}^{(4)}(s)|\leq B,$ and $|\phi_{i}^{(5)}(s)|\leq L.$

Assumption 3 (CRN) . For each index $i$ , the same example $\tau_{i}$ is used to evaluate $\{\phi_{i}(-\epsilon),\phi_{i}(0),\phi_{i}(\epsilon)\}.$ Moreover, for $i\neq j$ , the examples $\tau_{i}$ and $\tau_{j}$ are sampled independently.

Assumption 4 . (Sub-Gaussian Deviation) For each $\phi_{i},$ the directional deviations at $s=0$ are sub-gaussian up to third order, i.e., there exists constant $\sigma$ such that, for every $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and all $\lambda\in\mathbb{R},$ $\mathbb{E}[\exp(\lambda[\phi_{i}^{(k)}(0)-\psi^{(k)}(0)])]\leq\exp(\frac{\lambda^{2}\sigma^{2}}{2}).$

Theorem 1 (CRN curvature concentration) . Suppose Assumptions 1 – 4 hold. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$ , $\left|\widehat{\phi^{\prime\prime}}(0)-\psi^{\prime\prime}(0)\right|\leq\frac{B\epsilon^{2}}{12}+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(4/\delta)}{n}},$ and $\left|\widehat{\phi^{\prime\prime\prime}}(0)-\psi^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)\right|\leq\frac{L\epsilon^{2}}{20}+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(4/\delta)}{n}}.$

Theorem 2 (Second-order Taylor approximation bound) . Suppose Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Then the step selected by maximizing the second-order Taylor model satisfies $\phi(s_{M})\geq\phi(s_{\phi})-\frac{MR^{3}}{3}-\frac{B\epsilon^{2}R^{2}}{12}.$

Assumption 5 (Smooth and bounded objective) . The true objective $J:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ is $\mathcal{L}_{J}$ -smooth and bounded above by $J^{\star}$ . That is, for all $x,y$ , $J(y)\geq J(x)+\langle\nabla J(x),y-x\rangle-\frac{\mathcal{L}_{J}}{2}\|y-x\|^{2},$ and $J(\theta_{t})\leq J^{\star}$ for all iterations $t$ . Additionally, the expected surrogate $\bar{F}$ is also $\mathcal{L}_{\bar{F}}$ -smooth.
Assumption 6 (Aligned update direction) . There exists $\mu>0$ such that, for all $t$ , $q_{t}=\mathbb{E}_{t}[\langle\nabla J(\theta_{t}),z_{t}\rangle]\geq\mu\|\nabla J(\theta_{t})\|.$

Theorem 3 (Stationarity of the ZFO update) . Let Assumptions 5 – 6 hold and $q_{t}/\mathcal{L}_{J}\in I_{t}.$ Then, for every $T>0$ , with probability at least $1-\delta,$ we have $\min_{0\leq t\leq T}\mathbb{E}\|\nabla J(\theta_{t})\|^{2}\leq\frac{2\mathcal{L}_{J}(J^{\star}-J(\theta_{0}))}{\mu^{2}T}+\frac{2\mathcal{L}_{J}\tilde{\Delta}_{T}}{\mu^{2}},\text{ where }\tilde{\Delta}_{T}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{t}].$

Theorem 1 (CRN curvature concentration) . Suppose Assumptions 1 – 4 hold. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$ , $\left|\widehat{\phi^{\prime\prime}}(0)-\psi^{\prime\prime}(0)\right|\leq\frac{B\epsilon^{2}}{12}+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(4/\delta)}{n}},$ and $\left|\widehat{\phi^{\prime\prime\prime}}(0)-\psi^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)\right|\leq\frac{L\epsilon^{2}}{20}+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(4/\delta)}{n}}.$

Theorem 2 (Second-order Taylor approximation bound) . Suppose Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Then the step selected by maximizing the second-order Taylor model satisfies $\phi(s_{M})\geq\phi(s_{\phi})-\frac{MR^{3}}{3}-\frac{B\epsilon^{2}R^{2}}{12}.$

Definition 2 . Let $P_{k}(s)$ be the $k$ -th order Padé approximation of $\phi(s)$ over $[0,{R}]$ , where $P_{k}(s)=\frac{N(s)}{D(s)},N(s)=a_{0}+a_{1}s,$ with $D(s)=1+d_{1}s$ for $k=2$ and $D(s)=1+d_{1}s+d_{2}s^{2}$ for $k=3$ , and ${R}=s_{\rm FO}\beta,$ such that $\beta>0$ . The coefficients of $N(s)$ and $D(s)$ are chosen so that $P_{k}(s)$ agrees with the $k$ -th order Taylor model $T_{k}(s)$ when Taylor expanded. Define the Padé residual $r(s):=D(s)\phi(s)-N(s).$
Assumption 7 . The Padé denominator is bounded away from zero on $[0,{R}]$ , i.e., there exists $\eta>0$ such that $|D(s)|\geq\eta,\forall s\in[0,{R}],$ for both Padé 2 and Padé 3 .

Assumption 8 . The Padé residual has bounded higher-order derivatives, i.e., there exist $Q,P>0$ such that $|r^{(3)}(s)|\leq Q\quad\text{(Pad\'{e}${}_{2}$)},\quad|r^{(4)}(s)|\leq P\quad\text{(Pad\'{e}${}_{3}$)},\quad\forall s\in[0,{R}].$

Corollary 1 (Third-order Taylor approximation bound) . Suppose Assumptions 1 - 2 hold. Then the step selected by maximizing the third-order Taylor model satisfies $\phi(s_{M})\geq\phi(s_{\phi})-\frac{BR^{4}}{12}-\frac{B\epsilon^{2}R^{2}}{12}-\frac{L\epsilon^{2}R^{3}}{60}.$

Corollary 2 (Padé 2 approximation bound) . Let Assumptions 1 - 2 and 7 - 8 hold. Then the step selected by maximizing the Padé 2 model satisfies $\phi(s_{M})\geq\phi(s_{\phi})-\frac{B\epsilon^{2}{R}^{2}}{12\eta}-\frac{Q{R}^{3}}{3\eta}.$

Corollary 3 (Padé 3 approximation bound) . Let Assumptions 1 - 2 and 7 - 8 hold. Then the step selected by maximizing the Padé 3 model satisfies $\phi(s_{M})\geq\phi(s_{\phi})-\frac{B\epsilon^{2}{R}^{2}}{12\eta}-\frac{L\epsilon^{2}{R}^{3}}{60\eta}-\frac{|d_{1}|B\epsilon^{2}{R}^{3}}{12\eta}-\frac{P{R}^{4}}{12\eta}.$

Assumption 9 . Let the difference between the second derivative of $\phi$ and the second order approximation of $\phi$ at $s=0$ be bounded, i.e., there exists $D>0$ such that $|\phi^{\prime\prime}(s)-\frac{\phi(\epsilon)-2\phi(0)+\phi(-\epsilon)}{\epsilon^{2}}|\leq D;\forall s\in[0,{R}].$

Assumption 10 . Let $\phi$ be $
u$ -strongly concave on $[0,{R}]$ , i.e., $\phi(u)\leq\phi(s)+\phi^{\prime}(s)(u-s)- rac{
u}{2}(u-s)^{2};$ for all $s,u\in[0,{R}]$ where $
u>0.$

Assumption 11 . Let the maximum of $T_{2}(s)$ be an interior point, i.e., $-\frac{\epsilon^{2}\phi^{\prime}(0)}{\phi(\epsilon)-2\phi(0)+\phi(-\epsilon)}\in[0,{R}]$ and $\phi(\epsilon)-2\phi(0)+\phi(-\epsilon)<0$ .

Theorem 4 (Second-order Taylor win guarantee) . If Assumption 1 and Assumptions 9 - 11 hold, and if $s_{\rm FO}\in[0,{R}]$ , then the following relation holds between $\phi(s_{M})$ and $\phi(s_{\rm FO})$ : $\text{if }|s_{\rm FO}-s_{M}|=0\text{ or }|s_{\rm FO}-s_{M}|\geq\frac{2Ds_{M}}{\nu},\text{ then }\phi(s_{M})\geq\phi(s_{\rm FO}).$

Theorem 3 (Stationarity of the ZFO update) . Suppose Assumptions 5 – 6 hold. Assume also that $q_{t}/\mathcal{L}_{J}\in I_{t}.$ Then, for every $T>0$ , with probability at least $1-\delta,$ $\min_{0\leq t\leq T}\mathbb{E}\|\nabla J(\theta_{t})\|^{2}\leq\frac{2\mathcal{L}_{J}(J^{\star}-J(\theta_{0}))}{\mu^{2}T}+\frac{2\mathcal{L}_{J}\tilde{\Delta}_{T}}{\mu^{2}},\text{ where }\tilde{\Delta}_{T}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{t}].$
